newsitem.title: Iran: Velayati says Iran, Total in $3.5 bln gas deal.
newsitem.headline: Velayati says Iran, Total in $3.5 bln gas deal.

text.p: Iran's foreign minister said on Sunday Tehran had signed a $3.5 billion deal with France's Total to develop the South Pars gas field, despite threats of U.S. sanctions on foreign firms that invest in the republic.

"Total has signed an agreement with the minister of oil of our country. It belongs to South Pars which is an important field for gas production," Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati told a news conference. He said the deal was worth $3.5 billion.
But the National Iranian Oil Co (NIOC) denied that Iran had signed the deal with Total.
"The foreign minister's statement is not correct as such. NIOC and the Ministry of Petroleum have not finalised any agreement with either Total or Shell," said an NIOC official.
"Our negotiations with the two sides are still continuing," the official added.

Total's South Pars contract would be vulnerable to penalties under the Iran-Libya sanctions act which allows the U.S. president to penalise non-U.S. firms that invest $40 million or more a year in Iran's oil and gas sectors.
Velayati did not say when the deal was signed to develop the field which is expected to become the backbone of Iran's plans to export gas to Turkey, Pakistan, India and eventually Europe.
Iranian oil officials said earlier this month that two international consortia, led by Total and Royal Dutch/Shell, were in the race for the second and third phase of development of South Pars.
The field, which Iran shares with the Gulf Arab state of Qatar, is one of the world's single largest offshore gas fields.
Total vice president Christophe de Margerie said earlier this month during an energy conference in Isfahan that his company was keen to secure the deal under the right conditions.

Total is already developing Iran's offshore Sirri A and E oil and gas fields. The company has maintained close ties with the Islamic republic despite U.S. sanctions aimed at punishing foreign firms that invest in Iran.
